qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Abbott's economic moat rests on high customer switching barriers and consumable toll-booth dynamics across Medical Devices and Diagnostics. FreeStyle Libre commands >50% global CGM patient volume with >8 million active users purchasing recurring bi-weekly sensor replacements at >70% gross margins. In Diagnostics, closed-loop Alinity/Architect analyzers lock hospital laboratories into proprietary multi-year reagent consumable contracts. Structural heart franchises (MitraClip, TriClip, Navitor) benefit from extensive clinician procedural training and high switching costs. Empirical proof: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 12.8%, tangible operating ROIC >25-50%, gross margins consistently 55-57%, and FCF conversion of 80.6%. Primary erosion risks include competitive encroachment from Dexcom in CGM, GLP-1 therapy penetration moderating intensive diabetes therapies, and preterm infant formula product liability claims.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global diversified medtech and healthcare leader anchored by the FreeStyle Libre CGM franchise, structural heart devices, closed-loop diagnostic lab analyzers, and leading pediatric/adult nutrition brands. Highly insulated from AI disruption and a prime secular beneficiary of global demographic aging. Fortress balance sheet with net debt of just $1.4B (0.2x net income) and 16.3x interest coverage; $670M NEC infant formula settlement is comfortably absorbed by normal cash flow. [5-10Y g: FreeStyle Libre & medtech device volume 5.5% + diagnostic & nutrition pricing 1.5% + emerging markets pharma mix 1.0% - margin/litigation drag 0.5% + share repurchases 0.5%]
qualitative.evidence: Abbott generates >$44B in diversified revenue across Medical Devices ($17B+, led by $7.6B Libre CGM and structural heart), Diagnostics ($9B+ core lab/point-of-care), Nutrition ($8B+ Similac/Ensure), and Established Pharmaceuticals ($5B+ branded generics). Capital efficiency is verified by a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 12.8% and tangible operating ROIC of 53.3%. Free cash flow conversion averages 80.6% ($6.7B FCF in FY2025 on $6.5B Net Income). De-leveraging discipline is exemplary: debt reduced from $27.2B post-St. Jude in 2017 to $9.9B in FY2025, offset by $8.5B in cash (net debt $1.4B vs. $8.1B EBIT; interest coverage 16.3x). 52 consecutive years of dividend increases (Dividend King). Post-COVID testing normalization is complete, with organic core device and diagnostic volumes resuming high-single-digit peak-to-peak earnings expansion.
